newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki sturdied by Nokia and window-dressing.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki sturdied by Nokia and window-dressing.

text.p: Shares closed a fairly active session moderately higher on Monday, paring earlier losses on a late rally in Nokia and with some some help from window-dressing, brokers said.
The HEX index edged up 0.14 percent to 2,174.14. Volume was fairly sturdy at 317 million markka.
Nokia ended official trade 1.50 markka higher at 203.90, although it opened slightly lower on Wall Street. The share accounted for 36 percent of total bourse turnover.
Brokers spotted some end-of-month window-dressing, particularly in trading in smaller company shares.
Forestries remained subdued as worries mounted that planned pulp price hikes would not go through, brokers said.
"It seems highly unlikely now that producers can go ahead with the planned pulp price increases," one broker said.
Among forestries, UPM-Kymmene fell 0.80 markka to 95.20, and Enso shed 0.30 markka to end at 35.80. But Metsa-Serla bucked the trend rising 0.50 markka to 30.00.
Insurers remained well-bid on continuing talk of possible near-term restructuring of ownership in the sector.
Speculation has spread in the market that banking group Merita, which has major holdings in Pohjola and Sampo, might dispose of or reduce its stake in the insurance companies.
Sampo advanced 2.00 markka to 330.00, while Pohjola gained 0.70 markka to 93.50.
Beverages group Hartwall closed at an all-time high 150.00 markka, up seven, buoyed by its stronger-than-expected January-August results released last week.
